name: Author accessible components (WCAG 2.2 AA by construction)
desc: Build every component accessible from the start — semantics, name/role/value, keyboard + focus, contrast, and announced status — the author-time counterpart to the wcag-audit review skill.
body:
Author every component to WCAG 2.2 level AA BY CONSTRUCTION. This is the build-time counterpart to the `wcag-audit` review skill — bake accessibility in; don't wait for the audit to catch it. The app is a WebView, so each OS's own screen reader (VoiceOver / Narrator / NVDA / Orca) narrates the component by walking the DOM accessibility tree — correct semantics ARE the integration.
1. Semantics first: use the native element for its role — `<button>` for actions (NEVER `<div onClick>`), `<a href>` for navigation, `<nav>`/`<main>`/`<header>`/`<ul>`/`<li>`/`<h1..h6>` for structure, `<label>` bound to every input. Reach for ARIA only to fill a gap native HTML can't express (WCAG 4.1.2).
2. Name / role / value: every interactive element exposes an accessible NAME (a visible `<label>`, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`) and its STATE (`aria-expanded`/`selected`/`checked`/`disabled`/`current`). An icon-only control MUST carry an `aria-label`. Custom widgets follow the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices pattern for their role.
3. Keyboard + focus: everything operable by keyboard with no traps (2.1.1/2.1.2); tab and focus order match the visual order (2.4.3); a visible focus indicator (2.4.7); manage focus on open/close of modals, menus, and inboxes — move focus in on open, restore it on close.
4. Announce status: async and status changes (a worker paused, a save completed, a validation error) go through a LIVE REGION (`aria-live="polite"`, or `role="status"`/`"alert"`) so the screen reader announces them without stealing focus (4.1.3). This is the app's single biggest current gap — the whole app ships with one live region.
5. Perceivable: color is never the SOLE signal — pair it with text/icon/shape (1.4.1); text contrast >= 4.5:1 (>= 3:1 for large text / icons, 1.4.3); honor `prefers-reduced-motion`; interactive target >= 24x24px (2.5.8); layout reflows to 320px without loss (1.4.10).
6. Forms: programmatically associate label + input, describe requirements and errors via `aria-describedby`, and identify errors in TEXT, not color alone (3.3.1/3.3.2).
Prefer a shared primitive (a Button/Field/Dialog that already bakes these in) over re-solving per component. When done, run `wcag-audit` against the result to confirm.
